data.etymology: Lailaht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lailaht total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.name: Lailaht
in_english.meaning: Lailaht is an Arabic name derived from the root word for night
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lailaht is derived from the Arabic root word for night, which is a fundamental concept in Islamic tradition. The name Lailaht is a combination of the Arabic words لَيْل (layl) meaning night and حَت (hat) meaning new or fresh. In Islamic tradition, the night is a time for spiritual growth and reflection, and the name Lailaht is a reflection of this significance. The name Lailaht is also associated with the concept of tahajjud, which is the act of staying up late at night for prayer and spiritual reflection. In modern times, the name Lailaht has become popular in many Muslim cultures, and is often given to children in celebration of the beauty and significance of the night

data.cultural_impact: The name "Lailaht" has been mentioned in various Arabic and Islamic texts, including the poetry of the renowned Arab poet Imru' al-Qais and in some Hadiths, where it is believed to reference a companion of Prophet Muhammad SAW. The name holds a deep connection to Arabic culture, particularly in relation to night, as the concept of "Al-Laylah Al-Tarikhah" refers to the long, charged nights in the Arab desert, filled with stories, poems, and companionship. The name has also been used as a given name for newborns in Arab and Muslim communities, bringing a sense of nostalgia and connection to this rich cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spiritualism, the name "Lailaht" is believed to be a reminder of the deep spiritual significance of the night. In prayer and worship, Muslims are encouraged to seek nearness to Allah during the hours of the night, believing that the night is a time for increased spiritual connection and growth. The Prophet Muhammad SAW is reported to have said, "Take advantage of five blessings given to you: your youth, your good health, your leisure, your energy, and your happiness (or wealth)." The night represents one of these blessings, a time for spiritual reflection, prayer, and seeking knowledge. Therefore, the name "Lailaht" carries a deep spiritual significance, reminding the bearer of their potential to seek closeness to Allah and to embrace the spiritual blessings of the night.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Night" symbolizes The one who comes at night. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Lailaht serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of night.
